title: Smooth chart comparison for properties of Deligne--Mumford stack morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use Deligne--Mumford stacks, algebraic spaces, representability and 2-fibre products as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space, def-pc-fibre-product]. Smooth maps of algebraic spaces are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; smooth representable stack maps are tested after scheme base change. Let $\mathcal P$ be an isomorphism-invariant property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$. Suppose $\mathcal P$ is smooth local on source-and-target, meaning: (i) precomposing a map having $\mathcal P$ with a smooth map preserves $\mathcal P$; (ii) smooth base change preserves $\mathcal P$; (iii) a map $r:X\to Y$ of algebraic spaces has $\mathcal P$ if and only if for every field-valued point class $x\in|X|$ there is a commutative diagram $U\xrightarrow{h}V$ above $X\xrightarrow{r}Y$, with smooth vertical maps $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$ and a point $u\in|U|$ above $x$, for which $h$ has $\mathcal P$. Here point classes identify field maps that agree after a common field extension [def-weil-field]. For a morphism $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of Deligne--Mumford stacks, consider 2-commutative diagrams $U\xrightarrow{h}V$ above $f$, with $U,V$ algebraic spaces and smooth vertical maps $a:U\to\mathcal X$, $b:V\to\mathcal Y$. The following conditions are equivalent: (A) every such diagram whose induced map $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ is smooth has $\mathcal P(h)$; (B) there exists such a diagram with $a$ surjective and $\mathcal P(h)$. Requiring $U,V$ to be schemes in (A) and (B) gives the same conditions. If $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ are algebraic spaces, these conditions are also equivalent to $\mathcal P(f)$ for their ordinary map. If additionally arbitrary algebraic-space base change preserves $\mathcal P$ and $\mathcal P$ is fppf local on the target, then for $f$ representable by algebraic spaces, (A) and (B) are equivalent to $\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T\to T)$ for every scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$. Fppf local means that a map has $\mathcal P$ if and only if all its pullbacks by an fppf covering of its target have $\mathcal P$; coverings of spaces are tested on schemes using [def-pc-fppf-site].

source.place: Tag 06FM (lemma-local-source-target); smooth-local hypothesis as in spaces-descent.tex Tag 06F8 (definition-local-source-target). Scheme-chart version by etale atlas refinement. For the etale-stack convention, criteria.tex Tag 076V (lemma-stacks-etale).

proof.text: Write $A_{\mathrm{sp}},B_{\mathrm{sp}}$ for (A),(B) and $A_{\mathrm{sch}},B_{\mathrm{sch}}$ for their scheme-chart versions. The etale atlas in the definition of a Deligne--Mumford stack is smooth by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Thus [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent] applies: the diagonal is representable and the scheme atlas is smooth and surjective, so the etale stacks used here are also fppf algebraic stacks. We may use the cited stack base-change calculus with exactly the original stacks and 2-fibre products. All the vertical maps from spaces below are understood as representable by algebraic spaces, as in the statement's chart convention.

source.place: Tag 06FM, setting; criteria.tex Tag 076V (lemma-stacks-etale), etale/fppf convention

proof.text: Prove $A_{\mathrm{sch}}\Rightarrow B_{\mathrm{sch}}$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal Y$. By [lem-sfb-dm-etale-atlas-calculus], $Q=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ is Deligne--Mumford and has a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to Q$. The map $Q\to\mathcal X$ is the base change of $V\to\mathcal Y$, so its composite $a:U\to\mathcal X$ is smooth and surjective by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Both $b:V\to\mathcal Y$ and $U\to Q$ are smooth. Hence this is an admissible scheme diagram in (A); $A_{\mathrm{sch}}$ gives $\mathcal P(U\to V)$, proving $B_{\mathrm{sch}}$.

source.place: Tag 06FM, first proof paragraph: choose presentations of the target and its pullback

proof.text: Assume $B_{\mathrm{sp}}$, witnessed by $(U,V,a,b,h)$, and fix an arbitrary admissible diagram $(U',V',a',b',h')$ of $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$. Put $W=U\times_{\mathcal X}U'$, $D_0=V\times_{\mathcal Y}V'$ and $R_0=U\times_VD_0$. The first two are spaces by [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space], applied respectively to $a$ and $b$ with space bases $U'$ and $V'$; the third is a space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. There is a canonical identification $R_0\simeq U\times_{\mathcal Y}V'$. Set $Q'=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V'$. Then $W\simeq R_0\times_{Q'}U'$: on each scheme, both sides specify $u,u'$ and an isomorphism $a(u)\simeq a'(u')$, with the isomorphism to the $V'$-object determined by this and the two diagram 2-isomorphisms. Thus $W\to R_0$ is the base change of the assumed smooth map $U'\to Q'$. Moreover $W\to U'$ is the base change of $a$, hence smooth surjective; $D_0\to V'$ and $D_0\to V$ are the smooth base changes of $b$ and $b'$. These assertions use [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus].

source.place: Tag 06FM, converse: comparison diagram and the cartesian square above the middle column

proof.text: The map $R_0\to D_0$ is the smooth base change of $h$, so hypothesis (ii) gives $\mathcal P(R_0\to D_0)$. Since $W\to R_0$ is smooth, (i) gives $\mathcal P(W\to D_0)$. For each $u'\in|U'|$, surjectivity of $W\to U'$ supplies a point $w$ above it. The square $W\to D_0$ above $h':U'\to V'$ has smooth vertical arrows, so hypothesis (iii), using this $w$ for each $u'$, gives $\mathcal P(h')$. This proves $B_{\mathrm{sp}}\Rightarrow A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ directly from the assumed locality; no separate smooth-locality lemma or stability under arbitrary base change has been used.

source.place: Tag 06FM, converse, last four sentences; spaces-descent.tex Tag 06F8 (definition-local-source-target), clauses (i)--(iii)

proof.text: A scheme is an algebraic space by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], so $A_{\mathrm{sp}}\Rightarrow A_{\mathrm{sch}}$ and $B_{\mathrm{sch}}\Rightarrow B_{\mathrm{sp}}$ are restriction and inclusion of the chart classes. Together with steps 2--4, these give the cycle $A_{\mathrm{sp}}\Rightarrow A_{\mathrm{sch}}\Rightarrow B_{\mathrm{sch}}\Rightarrow B_{\mathrm{sp}}\Rightarrow A_{\mathrm{sp}}$, proving all four conditions equivalent. If $\mathcal X=X$ and $\mathcal Y=Y$ are spaces, $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ applied to $U=X,V=Y$ and the identity vertical maps gives $\mathcal P(f)$. Conversely, if $\mathcal P(f)$ holds, (ii) gives $\mathcal P(X\times_YV\to V)$ for any diagram in (A), and (i) gives $\mathcal P(h)$ after the assumed smooth map $U\to X\times_YV$.

source.place: Tag 06FM, representable-spaces paragraph; scheme version via scheme presentations in the first paragraph

proof.text: Assume now the additional hypotheses and that $f$ is representable by spaces. Given a scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$, put $Z=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T$, which is a space. For a witness to $B_{\mathrm{sp}}$, put $H=T\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ and $G_0=Z\times_{\mathcal X}U$. These are spaces by [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space], using the representable maps $b$ and $a$. The defining triples of the 2-fibre products identify $G_0$ with $T\times_{\mathcal Y}U$ and with $H\times_VU$. Thus $G_0\to H$ is the base change of $h$ along $H\to V$, so has $\mathcal P$ by arbitrary-base-change stability. In the square $G_0\to H$ above $Z\to T$, the vertical maps are respectively the base changes of $a$ and $b$; they are smooth, and the left one is surjective, by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Hypothesis (iii) at each point of $Z$ therefore gives $\mathcal P(Z\to T)$. The assumed fppf locality is not needed for this direction: the explicitly assumed pointwise source-and-target locality already gives the descent used here.

source.place: Tag 06FM, final proof paragraph: base change of the witness diagram by a scheme

proof.text: Conversely suppose $\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T\to T)$ for every scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to\mathcal Y$. Representability of $f$ makes $Z=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ a space, with $\mathcal P(Z\to V)$ by the assumption at $T=V$. Choose an etale surjective scheme atlas $U\to Z$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. It is smooth, so (i) gives $\mathcal P(h)$ for $h:U\to Z\to V$. The map $Z\to\mathcal X$ is a base change of the smooth surjective atlas $V\to\mathcal Y$; hence $U\to\mathcal X$ is smooth surjective by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. This is a scheme witness to (B), and completes the final equivalence.

source.place: Tag 06FM, representable compatibility; converse by the first paragraph's atlas construction
